source.text: שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י רֹ֥דְפֵי צֶ֖דֶק מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַבִּ֨יטוּ֙ אֶל־צ֣וּר חֻצַּבְתֶּ֔ם וְאֶל־מַקֶּ֥בֶת בּ֖וֹר נֻקַּרְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Listen to me, pursuers of righteousness, seekers of Yahweh: look to [the] rock [from which] you were hewn, and to [the] excavation of [the] pit [from which] you were dug out.

en.L: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, [you] pursuers of righteousness, seekers of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q look to the rock [from which] you were hewn, \q and to the quarry of the pit [from which] you were dug.
en.B: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who chase after righteousness, you who seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q look to the rock you were cut from, \q to the hollow of the pit you were dug out of.
en.R: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, all of you who want to do what is right and who turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Think about where you came from. \q You are like stone that was cut from a great rock, dug out of a deep quarry.

es.L: {{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, los que siguen la justicia, los que buscan {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: \q {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} a la roca [de donde] {{plural_you:fueron cortados|fuisteis cortados}}, \q y a la cantera del pozo [de donde] {{plural_you:fueron sacados|fuisteis sacados}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que van tras la justicia, que buscan {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: \q {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} la roca de la que {{plural_you:fueron cortados|fuisteis cortados}}, \q la cavidad del pozo del que {{plural_you:fueron extraídos|fuisteis extraídos}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, todos los que quieren hacer lo que es justo y se vuelven {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q {{plural_you:Piensen de dónde vienen|Pensad de dónde venís}}. \q {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} como piedra cortada de una gran roca, sacada de una cantera profunda.

sw.L: Nisikilizeni, [ninyi] mnaoifuata haki, mnaomtafuta {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: \q utazameni mwamba [ambao] mlichongwa kutoka kwake, \q na shimo la machimbo [ambamo] mlichimbuliwa.
sw.B: Nisikilizeni, ninyi mnaoikimbilia haki, ninyi mnaomtafuta {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: \q utazameni mwamba mlimokatwa, \q na tundu la shimo mlimochimbuliwa.
sw.R: Nisikilizeni, ninyi nyote mnaotaka kutenda yaliyo haki na mnaomgeukia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Fikirini mahali mlipotoka. \q Ninyi ni kama jiwe lililokatwa kutoka katika mwamba mkubwa, lililochimbuliwa katika machimbo marefu.

decisions.choice: the rock you were hewn from, the quarry you were dug from: the ancestors the people came from
decisions.reason: Verse 2 explains the picture: the rock and the quarry are Abraham and Sarah. As stone is cut from a quarry, the nation was cut from them.

decisions.choice: pursuers of righteousness: those who earnestly seek to live rightly, and to see God set things right
decisions.reason: Righteousness here is both right living and the right order God promises to bring (verses 5-8; Deuteronomy 16:20). The hearers are the faithful in Israel, who also "seek the LORD".

decisions.choice: want to do what is right; Think about where you came from
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what pursuing righteousness means and what the call to look at the rock is for.

source.text: הַבִּ֨יטוּ֙ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֣ם אֲבִיכֶ֔ם וְאֶל־שָׂרָ֖ה תְּחוֹלֶלְכֶ֑ם כִּי־אֶחָ֣ד קְרָאתִ֔יו וַאֲבָרְכֵ֖הוּ וְאַרְבֵּֽהוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah [who] bore you; for one I called him, and I blessed him and I multiplied him.

en.L: Look to Abraham your father \q and to Sarah [who] bore you; \q for [when he was but] one I called him, \q and I blessed him and multiplied him.
en.B: Look to Abraham your ancestor \q and to Sarah, who gave birth to your people. \q When I called him he was a single man, \q yet I blessed him and made him many.
en.R: Think about Abraham, your ancestor, \q and Sarah, the mother of your nation. \q When I chose Abraham, he was only one man. \q But I blessed him and gave him many descendants.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} a Abraham, {{plural_you:su padre|vuestro padre}}, \q y a Sara, [que] {{plural_you:los|os}} dio a luz; \q porque [siendo] uno solo lo llamé, \q y lo bendije y lo multipliqué.
es.B: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} a Abraham, {{plural_you:su antepasado|vuestro antepasado}}, \q y a Sara, que dio a luz a {{plural_you:su pueblo|vuestro pueblo}}. \q Cuando lo llamé, era un solo hombre, \q pero lo bendije y lo hice numeroso.
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en Abraham, {{plural_you:su antepasado|vuestro antepasado}}, \q y en Sara, la madre de {{plural_you:su nación|vuestra nación}}. \q Cuando escogí a Abraham, era solo un hombre. \q Pero lo bendije y le di muchos descendientes.

sw.L: Mtazameni Abrahamu baba yenu \q na Sara [aliyewazaa]; \q kwa maana [alipokuwa] mmoja nilimwita, \q nikambariki na kumwongeza.
sw.B: Mtazameni Abrahamu babu yenu, \q na Sara aliyewazaa watu wenu. \q Nilipomwita alikuwa mtu mmoja tu, \q lakini nilimbariki na kumfanya kuwa wengi.
sw.R: Mfikirieni Abrahamu, babu yenu, \q na Sara, mama wa taifa lenu. \q Nilipomchagua Abrahamu, alikuwa mtu mmoja tu. \q Lakini nilimbariki na kumpa wazao wengi.

decisions.choice: one I called, blessed and multiplied: the promise to Abraham in Genesis
decisions.reason: God called Abraham alone and promised to bless him and make him many (Genesis 12:1-3; 15:5; 22:17). Ezekiel 33:24 uses the same argument. If God made a nation from one man, he can rebuild the few left after the exile.

decisions.choice: your father, who bore you: the founding ancestors of the nation
decisions.reason: Abraham is "father" as ancestor; Sarah "bore you" as mother of the people through Isaac.

decisions.choice: your ancestor; gave birth to your people / the mother of your nation
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that Abraham and Sarah are the parents of the nation, not of each hearer.

source.text: כִּֽי־נִחַ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה צִיּ֗וֹן נִחַם֙ כָּל־חָרְבֹתֶ֔יהָ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם מִדְבָּרָהּ֙ כְּעֵ֔דֶן וְעַרְבָתָ֖הּ כְּגַן־יְהוָ֑ה שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יִמָּ֣צֵא בָ֔הּ תּוֹדָ֖ה וְק֥וֹל זִמְרָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For Yahweh will comfort Zion, he will comfort all her waste places, and he made her wilderness like Eden and her desert like [the] garden of Yahweh; joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and [the] sound of music.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will comfort Zion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will comfort all her ruins, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make her wilderness like Eden \q and her desert like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q joy and gladness will be found in her, \q thanksgiving and the sound of song.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will comfort Zion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring comfort to all her ruined places. \q He will make her wilderness like Eden, \q her barren plain like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Gladness and delight will be found in her, \q songs of thanks and the sound of music.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will comfort the people of Zion. He will comfort them in all the places that lie in ruins. \q He will make their dry land like the garden of Eden, \q like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q People there will be happy and glad. \q They will sing songs and thank God.

es.L: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} consolará a Sion; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} consolará todas sus ruinas, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hará su desierto como el Edén \q y su estepa como el huerto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; \q gozo y alegría se hallarán en ella, \q acción de gracias y voz de canto.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} consolará a Sion; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} traerá consuelo a todos sus lugares en ruinas. \q Hará que su desierto sea como el Edén, \q su llanura árida como el huerto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q En ella habrá alegría y gozo, \q cantos de gratitud y sonido de música.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} consolará al pueblo de Sion. Lo consolará en todos los lugares que están en ruinas. \q Hará que su tierra seca sea como el huerto del Edén, \q como el huerto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q La gente allí estará contenta y alegre. \q Cantarán canciones y darán gracias a Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataifariji Sayuni; atayafariji magofu yake yote, \q naye ataifanya nyika yake kama Edeni, \q na jangwa lake kama bustani ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q furaha na shangwe zitaonekana ndani yake, \q shukrani na sauti ya wimbo.
sw.B: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataifariji Sayuni; ataleta faraja kwa mahali pake pote palipoharibiwa. \q Ataifanya nyika yake kama Edeni, \q uwanda wake mkavu kama bustani ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Furaha na shangwe zitapatikana ndani yake, \q nyimbo za shukrani na sauti ya muziki.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atawafariji watu wa Sayuni. Atawafariji katika mahali pote palipo magofu. \q Ataifanya nchi yao kavu kama bustani ya Edeni, \q kama bustani ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Watu huko watakuwa na furaha na shangwe. \q Wataimba nyimbo na kumshukuru Mungu.

decisions.choice: will comfort, will make: the past-tense verbs describe what is certain to come
decisions.reason: The verbs are perfect forms, but the context looks forward: the prophet speaks of the coming restoration as if it were already done. The same certainty marks 40:1 and 52:9.

decisions.choice: like Eden, like the garden of the LORD: the first garden restored
decisions.reason: Eden is the garden God planted (Genesis 2:8-15; 13:10; Ezekiel 36:35). The ruined land will be made as fruitful and full of life as the first garden.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion; their dry land
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that comforting Zion means comforting her people, and joins the two parallel pictures of wilderness and desert.

source.text: הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ עַמִּ֔י וּלְאוּמִּ֖י אֵלַ֣י הַאֲזִ֑ינוּ כִּ֤י תוֹרָה֙ מֵאִתִּ֣י תֵצֵ֔א וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֔י לְא֥וֹר עַמִּ֖ים אַרְגִּֽיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Pay attention to me, my people, and my nation, to me give ear; for instruction from me will go out, and my justice to a light of peoples I will set at rest.

en.L: Pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} nation, give ear to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q for instruction will go out from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} justice I will set as a light for [the] peoples.
en.B: Listen closely to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people; \q hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} nation. \q Instruction will go out from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and I will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} justice stand firm as a light for the peoples.
en.R: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q Pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} nation. \q I will give {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching, and it will go out to the world. \q I will set up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} justice, and it will be a light for all nations.

es.L: {{plural_you:Préstenme|Prestadme}} atención, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nación, {{plural_you:denme|dadme}} oído; \q porque de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} saldrá la instrucción, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} justicia estableceré como luz de los pueblos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} con atención, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo; \q {{plural_you:óiganme|oídme}}, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nación. \q De {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} saldrá la instrucción, \q y haré que {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} justicia se mantenga firme como luz para los pueblos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}}, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. \q {{plural_you:Préstenme|Prestadme}} atención, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nación. \q Daré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enseñanza, y llegará a todo el mundo. \q Estableceré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} justicia, y será una luz para todas las naciones.

sw.L: Nisikilizeni, watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, \q na taifa {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, nitegeeni sikio; \q kwa maana mafundisho yatatoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, \q na hukumu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} nitaiweka kuwa nuru ya watu wa mataifa.
sw.B: Nisikilizeni kwa makini, watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; \q nisikieni, taifa {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. \q Mafundisho yatatoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, \q nami nitaifanya haki {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} isimame imara kama nuru kwa mataifa.
sw.R: Nisikilizeni, watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Nisikilizeni kwa makini, taifa {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. \q Nitatoa mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nayo yataenea ulimwenguni. \q Nitaisimamisha haki {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nayo itakuwa nuru kwa mataifa yote.

decisions.choice: instruction will go out, a light for the peoples: God's teaching and justice reaching all nations
decisions.reason: The words echo 2:3, where instruction goes out from Zion to the nations, and 42:4, 6 and 49:6, where the servant brings justice and is a light to the nations.

decisions.choice: I will set at rest: I will establish it firmly
decisions.reason: The verb means to give rest or settle (Jeremiah 31:2). The same root is also used of something done in a moment (Jeremiah 49:19), and some read it as "in a moment", joined to verse 5: "In a moment my righteousness is near."

decisions.choice: it will go out to the world; all nations
decisions.reason: Readable says where the teaching goes, as the parallel line about the peoples implies.

decisions.choice: hukumu yangu (Literal); haki yangu (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Justice" (mishpat) is "hukumu" at Literal and "haki" at Balanced and Readable through chapters 41-66, except in 42:1-4, where Matthew 12 has "haki" at every level.

source.text: קָר֤וֹב צִדְקִי֙ יָצָ֣א יִשְׁעִ֔י וּזְרֹעַ֖י עַמִּ֣ים יִשְׁפֹּ֑טוּ אֵלַי֙ אִיִּ֣ים יְקַוּ֔וּ וְאֶל־זְרֹעִ֖י יְיַחֵלֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: Near [is] my righteousness, has gone out my salvation, and my arms peoples will judge; to me islands will wait, and to my arm they will wait.

en.L: Near [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation has gone out, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arms will judge [the] peoples; \q the coastlands will wait for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arm they will hope.
en.B: My righteousness is close; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation has set out, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arms will judge the peoples. \q The coastlands look to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in hope, \q and they wait for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arm.
en.R: I will soon set things right. I am already on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} way to save. \q With {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power I will judge the nations. \q Lands far away are waiting for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They hope I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power for them.

es.L: Cerca [está] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} justicia; ha salido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} salvación, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} brazos juzgarán a los pueblos; \q las costas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} esperarán, \q y en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} brazo pondrán su esperanza.
es.B: Mi justicia está cerca; {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} salvación se ha puesto en camino, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} brazos juzgarán a los pueblos. \q Las costas lejanas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} miran con esperanza \q y aguardan {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} brazo.
es.R: Pronto pondré las cosas en orden. Ya estoy en camino para salvar. \q Con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} poder juzgaré a las naciones. \q Las tierras lejanas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} están esperando. \q Esperan que use {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} poder a su favor.

sw.L: Haki {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} [iko] karibu; wokovu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} umetoka, \q na mikono {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itawahukumu watu wa mataifa; \q visiwa vitaningojea, \q na mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} vitautumainia.
sw.B: Haki {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} iko karibu; wokovu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} umeanza safari, \q na mikono {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itawahukumu watu wa mataifa. \q Pwani za mbali zinanitazamia kwa matumaini, \q nazo zinaungoja mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.R: Hivi karibuni nitaweka mambo sawa. Tayari niko njiani kuokoa. \q Kwa uweza {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} nitayahukumu mataifa. \q Nchi za mbali ng'ambo ya bahari zinanisubiri. \q Zinatumaini kwamba nitatumia uweza {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kwa ajili yao.

decisions.choice: my righteousness: God's saving justice, his setting things right
decisions.reason: Set beside "my salvation", righteousness here is God acting to put right what is wrong and to rescue his people, as in 46:13 and 56:1.

decisions.choice: my arms, my arm: God's power in action
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength used for a task (40:10; 52:10; 53:1). The arms that judge also save: the coastlands wait for that arm in hope.

decisions.choice: will judge the peoples: rule them with justice
decisions.reason: To judge here is to govern and set right, not only to condemn (2:4; Psalm 96:13).

decisions.choice: I will soon set things right; I am on my way to save; with my power
decisions.reason: Readable turns the nouns into what God does and explains the arm as power.

source.text: שְׂאוּ֩ לַשָּׁמַ֨יִם עֵֽינֵיכֶ֜ם וְֽהַבִּ֧יטוּ אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ מִתַּ֗חַת כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֜יִם כֶּעָשָׁ֤ן נִמְלָ֨חוּ֙ וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ כַּבֶּ֣גֶד תִּבְלֶ֔ה וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כְּמוֹ־כֵ֣ן יְמוּת֑וּן וִישֽׁוּעָתִי֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְצִדְקָתִ֖י לֹ֥א תֵחָֽת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Lift up to the heavens your eyes, and look to the earth from beneath; for [the] heavens like smoke will be dispersed, and the earth like a garment will wear out, and its inhabitants like gnat[s] will die; and my salvation forever will be, and my righteousness not will be shattered.

en.L: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look to the earth beneath; \q for the heavens will vanish like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment, \q and its inhabitants will die like gnats; \q but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation will be forever, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness will not be shattered.
en.B: Raise your eyes to the sky and look at the earth below. \q The sky will drift away like smoke, the earth will fray like old clothing, \q and those who live on it will die like gnats. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation will remain forever, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness will never give way.
en.R: Look up at the sky, and look down at the earth. The sky will disappear like smoke. The earth will wear out like old clothes. \q The people who live on it will die like tiny insects. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation will last forever. \q My power to set things right will never fail.

es.L: {{plural_you:Alcen sus|Alzad vuestros}} ojos a los cielos, y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} la tierra abajo; \q porque los cielos se desvanecerán como humo, y la tierra se gastará como un vestido, \q y sus habitantes morirán como mosquitos; \q pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} salvación será para siempre, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} justicia no será quebrantada.
es.B: {{plural_you:Levanten|Levantad}} los ojos al cielo y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} la tierra abajo. \q El cielo se disipará como humo, la tierra se deshilachará como ropa vieja, \q y los que viven en ella morirán como mosquitos. \q Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} salvación permanecerá para siempre, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} justicia nunca cederá.
es.R: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} hacia arriba, al cielo, y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} hacia abajo, a la tierra. El cielo desaparecerá como el humo. La tierra se gastará como ropa vieja. \q La gente que vive en ella morirá como insectos diminutos. \q Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} salvación durará para siempre. \q Mi poder para poner las cosas en orden nunca fallará.

sw.L: Inueni macho yenu mbinguni, mkaitazame dunia chini; \q kwa maana mbingu zitatoweka kama moshi, na dunia itachakaa kama vazi, \q na wakaao ndani yake watakufa kama chawa; \q lakini wokovu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} utakuwa milele, \q na haki {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} haitavunjika.
sw.B: Inueni macho yenu mtazame anga, mkaitazame dunia iliyo chini. \q Anga litapeperuka kama moshi, dunia itachakaa kama nguo kuukuu, \q na wakaao juu yake watakufa kama mbu. \q Lakini wokovu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} utadumu milele, \q na haki {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} haitashindwa kamwe.
sw.R: Tazameni juu angani, na tazameni chini duniani. Anga litatoweka kama moshi. Dunia itachakaa kama nguo kuukuu. \q Watu wanaoishi juu yake watakufa kama wadudu wadogo. \q Lakini wokovu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} utadumu milele. \q Uweza {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kuweka mambo sawa hautashindwa kamwe.

decisions.choice: like gnats: like tiny insects that die in swarms
decisions.reason: The phrase can be read as one word meaning "in the same way", or as "like a gnat", from a word for small insects (compare Exodus 8:12-14). The second gives a picture that fits the smoke and the garment.

decisions.choice: the heavens and earth pass away, but God's salvation lasts forever
decisions.reason: Even the created world is temporary compared with what God does to save (Psalm 102:26-28; Hebrews 1:10-12). Isaiah also speaks of new heavens and a new earth (65:17; 66:22).

decisions.choice: My power to set things right will never fail
decisions.reason: Readable explains God's righteousness here as his setting things right, as in verse 5.

source.text: שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ יֹ֣דְעֵי צֶ֔דֶק עַ֖ם תּוֹרָתִ֣י בְלִבָּ֑ם אַל־תִּֽירְאוּ֙ חֶרְפַּ֣ת אֱנ֔וֹשׁ וּמִגִּדֻּפֹתָ֖ם אַל־תֵּחָֽתּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Listen to me, knowers of righteousness, a people [with] my instruction in their heart; do not fear [the] reproach of humankind, and from their revilings do not be dismayed.

en.L: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, [you] who know righteousness, \q [the] people [with] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction in their heart: \q do not fear [the] scorn of mortals, \q and do not be shattered by their insults.
en.B: Hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who know what is right, \q you people who carry {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction in your hearts: \q do not be afraid when mortals mock you, \q and do not lose heart at their abuse.
en.R: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who know what is right. \q You keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching in your hearts. \q Do not be afraid when people make fun of you. \q Do not be upset when they insult you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, los que conocen la justicia, \q pueblo [con] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} instrucción en su corazón: \q no {{plural_you:teman|temáis}} el oprobio de los mortales, \q ni {{plural_you:se quebranten|os quebrantéis}} por sus insultos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Óiganme|Oídme}}, {{plural_you:ustedes que conocen|vosotros que conocéis}} lo que es justo, \q pueblo que lleva {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} instrucción en el corazón: \q no {{plural_you:tengan miedo cuando los mortales se burlen de ustedes|tengáis miedo cuando los mortales se burlen de vosotros}}, \q ni {{plural_you:se desanimen|os desaniméis}} por sus ofensas.
es.R: {{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, {{plural_you:ustedes que saben|vosotros que sabéis}} lo que es justo. \q {{plural_you:Guardan|Guardáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enseñanza en el corazón. \q No {{plural_you:tengan miedo cuando la gente se burle de ustedes|tengáis miedo cuando la gente se burle de vosotros}}. \q No {{plural_you:se aflijan cuando los insulten|os aflijáis cuando os insulten}}.

sw.L: Nisikilizeni, [ninyi] mnaoijua haki, \q watu [wenye] mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mioyoni mwao: \q msiogope lawama za wanadamu, \q wala msivunjike kwa matukano yao.
sw.B: Nisikieni, ninyi mnaojua yaliyo haki, \q ninyi watu mnaoyabeba mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mioyoni mwenu: \q msiogope wanadamu wanapowadhihaki, \q wala msife moyo kwa matusi yao.
sw.R: Nisikilizeni, ninyi mnaojua yaliyo haki. \q Mnayaweka mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mioyoni mwenu. \q Msiogope watu wanapowadhihaki. \q Msihuzunike wanapowatukana.

decisions.choice: my instruction in their heart: God's teaching taken in and loved
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 6:6 and Psalm 37:31 speak of God's instruction on the heart; Jeremiah 31:33 promises a covenant in which God writes it there.

decisions.choice: mortals: human beings as weak and passing
decisions.reason: The word for humankind here stresses frailty. Verse 8 shows why their scorn need not be feared: they will be eaten like cloth (compare verse 12).

decisions.choice: know what is right
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express knowing righteousness as knowing what is right, since the line speaks of the people's way of life.

source.text: כִּ֤י כַבֶּ֨גֶד֙ יֹאכְלֵ֣ם עָ֔שׁ וְכַצֶּ֖מֶר יֹאכְלֵ֣ם סָ֑ס וְצִדְקָתִי֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וִישׁוּעָתִ֖י לְד֥וֹר דּוֹרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For like a garment a moth will eat them, and like wool a clothes-moth will eat them; and my righteousness forever will be, and my salvation to a generation of generations.

en.L: For like a garment the moth will eat them, \q and like wool the worm will eat them; \q but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness will be forever, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation to generation [after] generation.
en.B: Like clothing, they will be eaten by moths; \q like wool, they will be chewed by grubs. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness will stand forever, \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation through every generation.
en.R: Moths will eat them up like clothes. \q Worms will eat them like wool. \q But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power to set things right will last forever. \q I will save {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people in every generation.

es.L: Porque como a vestido los comerá la polilla, \q y como a lana los comerá el gusano; \q pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} justicia será para siempre, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} salvación por generación [y] generación.
es.B: Como a la ropa, se los comerán las polillas; \q como a la lana, los roerán las larvas. \q Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} justicia permanecerá para siempre, \q {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} salvación por todas las generaciones.
es.R: Las polillas se los comerán como a la ropa. \q Los gusanos se los comerán como a la lana. \q Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} poder para poner las cosas en orden durará para siempre. \q Salvaré a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo en cada generación.

sw.L: Kwa maana nondo atawala kama vazi, \q na funza atawala kama sufu; \q lakini haki {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itakuwa milele, \q na wokovu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kizazi [hata] kizazi.
sw.B: Kama nguo, wataliwa na nondo; \q kama sufu, watatafunwa na funza. \q Lakini haki {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itasimama milele, \q wokovu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} katika kila kizazi.
sw.R: Nondo watawala kama nguo. \q Funza watawala kama sufu. \q Lakini uweza {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kuweka mambo sawa utadumu milele. \q Nitawaokoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} katika kila kizazi.

decisions.choice: moth, clothes-moth: insects whose larvae eat cloth
decisions.reason: The second word is a rarer term for the moth or its grub that eats wool. Both lines picture the mockers wasting away (50:9).

decisions.choice: my righteousness forever, my salvation to all generations
decisions.reason: Verse 6 closes the same way, with the two words in the other order. The repetition frames verses 6-8: what God does to save will outlast everything that opposes it.

decisions.choice: my power to set things right; I will save my people
decisions.reason: Readable explains righteousness as in verse 6 and turns salvation into what God does.

source.text: עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י לִבְשִׁי־עֹז֙ זְר֣וֹעַ יְהוָ֔ה ע֚וּרִי כִּ֣ימֵי קֶ֔דֶם דֹּר֖וֹת עוֹלָמִ֑ים הֲל֥וֹא אַתְּ־הִ֛יא הַמַּחְצֶ֥בֶת רַ֖הַב מְחוֹלֶ֥לֶת תַּנִּֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of Yahweh; awake as [in] days of antiquity, generations of ages; [are] you not she [who] cut in pieces Rahab, [who] pierced [the] sea monster?

en.L: Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Awake as [in] days of old, [the] generations of long ago! \q [Was it] not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who hacked Rahab in pieces, \q who pierced the sea monster?
en.B: Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Awake as in days long gone, in ages past! \q Was it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who cut Rahab to pieces, \q who ran the sea monster through?
en.R: Wake up! Wake up, arm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Put on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength! \q Wake up as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did long ago, in the days of our ancestors. \q Was it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who cut Rahab into pieces? \q You stabbed that sea monster.

es.L: ¡Despierta, despierta, vístete de poder, brazo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q ¡Despierta como en los días antiguos, [en] las generaciones de antaño! \q ¿No [fuiste] {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quien despedazó a Rahab, \q quien traspasó al monstruo marino?
es.B: ¡Despierta, despierta, vístete de fuerza, brazo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q ¡Despierta como en los días de antaño, en las edades pasadas! \q ¿No fuiste {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quien hizo pedazos a Rahab, \q quien atravesó al monstruo marino?
es.R: ¡Despierta! ¡Despierta, brazo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! ¡Vístete de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fuerza! \q Despierta como lo hiciste hace mucho tiempo, en los días de nuestros antepasados. \q ¿No fuiste {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quien cortó en pedazos a Rahab? \q Tú apuñalaste a ese monstruo marino.

sw.L: Amka, amka, jivike nguvu, mkono wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Amka kama [katika] siku za kale, vizazi vya zamani! \q [Je,] si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyemkata Rahabu vipande vipande, \q uliyemchoma joka la baharini?
sw.B: Amka, amka, jivike nguvu, mkono wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Amka kama siku zilizopita, katika nyakati za kale! \q Je, si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyemkatakata Rahabu, \q uliyemtoboa joka la baharini?
sw.R: Amka! Amka, mkono wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Jivike nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}! \q Amka kama ulivyofanya zamani, katika siku za babu zetu. \q Je, si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyemkata Rahabu vipande vipande? \q Ulilichoma joka lile la baharini.

decisions.choice: awake, arm of the LORD: a cry to God to act with his power, as if he were asleep
decisions.reason: The people call on the LORD's arm, his power in action (verse 5; 53:1), as one wakes a sleeper (Psalm 44:24). The arm is God himself acting, so the words addressed to it are words to God. Later God turns the cry back on Jerusalem: "Rouse yourself" (verse 17; 52:1).

decisions.choice: Rahab, the sea monster: the monster of the sea, and a name for Egypt
decisions.reason: Rahab is a sea monster whom God defeats (Job 26:12; Psalm 89:11), and the same name is used for Egypt (30:7; Psalm 87:4). The sea monster is also named in 27:1. Verse 10 shows the sense: God's victory over the sea at the exodus was a victory over Egypt. The name is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: as in days of old: as God acted at the exodus
decisions.reason: The prayer asks God to act again as he did when he brought Israel out of Egypt (63:11-13; Psalm 77:6, 12-21).

decisions.choice: in the days of our ancestors; that sea monster
decisions.reason: Readable explains "generations of long ago" and links the monster to Rahab.

decisions.choice: Rahab; el monstruo marino
decisions.reason: The name Rahab is kept, as the English keeps it, and the second word is "monstruo marino", the sea monster defeated by God (Psalm 89:11; Job 26:12).

decisions.choice: Rahabu; joka la baharini
decisions.reason: Rahab, the monster of the sea and a name for Egypt (meaning decision m2), keeps its Swahili form as a name; it is not Rahab of Jericho, whose name differs in Hebrew though Swahili spells both "Rahabu".

source.text: הֲל֤וֹא אַתְּ־הִיא֙ הַמַּחֲרֶ֣בֶת יָ֔ם מֵ֖י תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֑ה הַשָּׂ֨מָה֙ מַֽעֲמַקֵּי־יָ֔ם דֶּ֖רֶךְ לַעֲבֹ֥ר גְּאוּלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [Are] you not she [who] dried up [the] sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of [the] sea a way to pass over [for the] redeemed?

en.L: [Was it] not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who dried up the sea, \q the waters of the great deep, \q who made the depths of the sea a road for the redeemed to cross?
en.B: Was it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who drained the sea, \q the waters of the vast deep, \q and turned the sea's depths into a road for the redeemed to cross?
en.R: Was it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who dried up the sea and the deep waters? \q You made a road through the bottom of the sea, \q so that the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bought back could walk across.

es.L: ¿No [fuiste] {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quien secó el mar, \q las aguas del gran abismo, \q quien hizo de las profundidades del mar un camino para que pasaran los redimidos?
es.B: ¿No fuiste {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quien dejó seco el mar, \q las aguas del inmenso abismo, \q y convirtió las profundidades del mar en un camino para que cruzaran los redimidos?
es.R: ¿No fuiste {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quien secó el mar y las aguas profundas? \q Hiciste un camino por el fondo del mar, \q para que el pueblo que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} rescataste pudiera cruzar.

sw.L: [Je,] si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyeikausha bahari, \q maji ya vilindi vikuu, \q uliyeyafanya mavilindi ya bahari kuwa njia ya waliokombolewa kuvuka?
sw.B: Je, si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyeikausha bahari, \q maji ya kilindi kikuu, \q na kuvigeuza vilindi vya bahari kuwa barabara ya waliokombolewa kuvuka?
sw.R: Je, si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyeikausha bahari na maji yake marefu? \q Ulifanya barabara chini kabisa ya bahari, \q ili watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} uliowanunua tena wapate kuvuka.

decisions.choice: dried up the sea, a way for the redeemed to cross: the crossing of the sea in the exodus
decisions.reason: God dried up the sea and his people walked through it (Exodus 14:21-22, 29; 15:13, 16). The great deep recalls the waters of creation and the flood (Genesis 1:2; 7:11).

decisions.choice: the redeemed: those God bought back, as a kinsman frees a relative
decisions.reason: The word is used of God's redeeming Israel from Egypt (Exodus 6:6; 15:13) and of the return from Babylon (35:9; 43:1).

decisions.choice: the people you bought back
decisions.reason: Readable explains "redeemed" with the settled wording for this verb.

source.text: וּפְדוּיֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה יְשׁוּב֗וּן וּבָ֤אוּ צִיּוֹן֙ בְּרִנָּ֔ה וְשִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם עַל־רֹאשָׁ֑ם שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יַשִּׂיג֔וּן נָ֖סוּ יָג֥וֹן וַאֲנָחָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the ransomed of Yahweh will return and come [to] Zion with a shout of joy, and everlasting gladness [will be] upon their head; joy and gladness will overtake [them]; sorrow and sighing will flee.

en.L: And [the] ransomed of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will return and come [to] Zion with a shout of joy, \q and everlasting joy [will be] upon their heads; \q gladness and joy will overtake [them], \q [and] sorrow and sighing will flee.
en.B: Those {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has ransomed will come back; they will enter Zion with glad shouts, \q with joy that never ends resting on their heads. \q Delight and gladness will catch up with them, \q and grief and groaning will run away.
en.R: The people {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has set free will come home. They will enter Zion singing and shouting. \q Their joy will last forever, and everyone will see it on them. \q Happiness and joy will catch up with them. \q Sadness and crying will run away.

es.L: Y [los] rescatados {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} volverán y vendrán a Sion con gritos de júbilo, \q y alegría eterna [habrá] sobre sus cabezas; \q gozo y alegría alcanzarán, \q [y] huirán la tristeza y el gemido.
es.B: Los que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha rescatado volverán; entrarán en Sion con gritos de alegría, \q con un gozo sin fin sobre la cabeza. \q El regocijo y la alegría los alcanzarán, \q y la tristeza y el gemido huirán.
es.R: La gente que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha liberado volverá a casa. Entrarán en Sion cantando y gritando. \q Su alegría durará para siempre, y todos la verán en ellos. \q La felicidad y la alegría los alcanzarán. \q La tristeza y el llanto huirán.

sw.L: Na waliokombolewa na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} watarudi na kuja Sayuni kwa kelele za furaha, \q na furaha ya milele [itakuwa] juu ya vichwa vyao; \q shangwe na furaha zitawapata, \q [na] huzuni na kuugua vitakimbia.
sw.B: Wale ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewakomboa watarudi; wataingia Sayuni kwa kelele za furaha, \q furaha isiyo na mwisho ikiwa juu ya vichwa vyao. \q Shangwe na furaha zitawafikia, \q na huzuni na kuugua vitakimbia.
sw.R: Watu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewaweka huru watarudi nyumbani. Wataingia Sayuni wakiimba na kupiga kelele za furaha. \q Furaha yao itadumu milele, na kila mtu ataiona juu yao. \q Furaha na shangwe zitawafikia. \q Huzuni na kilio vitakimbia.

decisions.choice: the ransomed of the LORD will return: the same words as 35:10
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 35:10 almost word for word (see the notes there on "ransomed", the joy on their heads and the joy that overtakes them). After the memory of the exodus in verse 10, the return from exile is pictured as a new exodus.

decisions.choice: sorrow and sighing will flee: the verb has no "and" before it here
decisions.reason: In 35:10 the last line begins with "and"; here it does not. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: Those the LORD has ransomed / The people the LORD has set free
decisions.reason: The wording follows 35:10, which has the same Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the wording of 35:10 at each level
decisions.reason: The verse repeats Isaiah 35:10, so each level keeps the same Spanish; only Literal's "[y] huirán" differs, because here the Hebrew has no "and".

decisions.choice: wording of 35:10 at every level; Literal brackets "[na]" before the last line
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 35:10 (meaning decision m1), so each level takes the Swahili of 35:10; the only Hebrew difference, the missing "and" before "sorrow and sighing" (meaning decision m2), shows as a bracket at Literal.

source.text: אָנֹכִ֧י אָנֹכִ֛י ה֖וּא מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם מִֽי־אַ֤תְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ מֵאֱנ֣וֹשׁ יָמ֔וּת וּמִבֶּן־אָדָ֖ם חָצִ֥יר יִנָּתֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: I, I [am] he [who] comforts you; who [are] you, and you have been afraid of a person [who] dies, and of a son of humankind [who] is made [like] grass?

en.L: I, I [am] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who comforts you. \q Who [are] you, that you are afraid of a man [who] dies, \q and of a son of man [who] is made [like] grass,
en.B: I, I am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who comforts you. \q Who are you, to be afraid of mortals who die, \q of human beings who wither like grass,
en.R: I myself am the one who comforts you. \q So why are you afraid of people? \q They are only human. They will die and dry up like grass.

es.L: Yo, yo [soy] {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, el que {{plural_you:los|os}} consuela. \q ¿Quién [eres] tú para temer al hombre [que] muere, \q y al hijo de hombre [que] es como la hierba,
es.B: Yo, yo soy {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, el que {{plural_you:los|os}} consuela. \q ¿Quién eres tú, para tener miedo de los mortales que mueren, \q de los seres humanos que se marchitan como la hierba,
es.R: Yo mismo soy el que {{plural_you:los|os}} consuela. \q Entonces, ¿por qué tienes miedo de la gente? \q No son más que seres humanos. Morirán y se secarán como la hierba.

sw.L: Mimi, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye nikufarijiye. \q Wewe [ni] nani, hata uogope mtu [ambaye] hufa, \q na mwanadamu [ambaye] hufanywa [kama] majani,
sw.B: Mimi, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye ninayewafariji. \q Wewe ni nani, hata uwaogope wanadamu wanaokufa, \q binadamu wanaonyauka kama majani,
sw.R: Mimi {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ndiye ninayewafariji. \q Basi kwa nini mnawaogopa watu? \q Wao ni binadamu tu. Watakufa na kukauka kama majani.

decisions.choice: I, I am he who comforts you: God alone is the comforter of his people
decisions.reason: The doubled "I" with "he" echoes the claim "I am he" (see the note at 43:10; 43:25). Here it is joined to comfort, picking up 40:1 and verse 3.

decisions.choice: a son of man made like grass: a mortal, who withers and dies
decisions.reason: "Son of man" means a human being. Grass that dries up pictures how short human life is (40:6-8; Psalm 103:15-16).

decisions.choice: who are you: the question is to Zion, and runs on into verse 13
decisions.reason: "You" is feminine here, Zion as a woman; in verse 13 it turns masculine, the people. The question asks how they can fear mortals and forget their Maker.

decisions.choice: I myself am the one who comforts you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the stress of the doubled "I" in plain words; this is not the absolute "I am he" of 43:10, so the wording "I alone am God" is not used here.

decisions.choice: a man ... a son of man / mortals ... human beings
decisions.reason: The two words mean human beings, men and women alike. Balanced uses inclusive words; Literal keeps the form "son of man" so the reader can see the idiom.

source.text: וַתִּשְׁכַּ֞ח יְהוָ֣ה עֹשֶׂ֗ךָ נוֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַיִם֮ וְיֹסֵ֣ד אָרֶץ֒ וַתְּפַחֵ֨ד תָּמִ֜יד כָּל־הַיּ֗וֹם מִפְּנֵי֙ חֲמַ֣ת הַמֵּצִ֔יק כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר כּוֹנֵ֖ן לְהַשְׁחִ֑ית וְאַיֵּ֖ה חֲמַ֥ת הַמֵּצִֽיק׃

records.literal_gloss: and you have forgotten Yahweh [who] made you, [who] stretched out [the] heavens and founded [the] earth, and you have been in dread continually all the day from before the fury of the oppressor, when he has prepared to destroy? And where [is] the fury of the oppressor?

en.L: and you have forgotten {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your Maker, [who] stretched out [the] heavens and founded [the] earth, \q and you dread continually all day long the fury of the oppressor, \q as he makes ready to destroy? \q And where [is] the fury of the oppressor?
en.B: and you have forgotten {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your Maker, who spread out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth? \q Day after day you live in constant dread of the oppressor's rage \q as he takes aim to destroy. \q But where is the oppressor's rage now?
en.R: You have forgotten {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who made you. He spread out the sky and made the earth firm. \q But all day long you are terrified of the angry person who is crushing you \q and getting ready to destroy you. \q Where is that anger now? It is gone!

es.L: y te has olvidado {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, tu Hacedor, [que] extendió los cielos y fundó la tierra, \q y temes continuamente todo el día el furor del opresor, \q cuando se dispone a destruir? \q ¿Y dónde [está] el furor del opresor?
es.B: y te has olvidado {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, tu Hacedor, que desplegó los cielos y puso los cimientos de la tierra? \q Día tras día vives con miedo constante de la furia del opresor \q mientras se prepara para destruir. \q Pero ¿dónde está ahora la furia del opresor?
es.R: Te has olvidado {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que te hizo. Él extendió el cielo y afirmó la tierra. \q Pero todo el día estás aterrado por la persona enojada que te aplasta \q y se prepara para destruirte. \q ¿Dónde está ahora ese enojo? ¡Ya no existe!

sw.L: nawe umemsahau {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Muumba wako, [aliyezitandaza] mbingu na kuiweka misingi ya dunia, \q nawe unaogopa daima mchana kutwa ghadhabu ya mdhalimu, \q anapojiandaa kuangamiza? \q Nayo iko wapi ghadhabu ya mdhalimu?
sw.B: nawe umemsahau {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Muumba wako, aliyezitandaza mbingu na kuiweka dunia juu ya misingi yake? \q Siku baada ya siku unaishi kwa hofu ya daima ya ghadhabu ya mdhalimu \q anapolenga kuangamiza. \q Lakini iko wapi sasa ghadhabu ya mdhalimu?
sw.R: Mmemsahau {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyewaumba. Yeye alizitandaza mbingu na kuifanya dunia imara. \q Lakini mchana kutwa mnamwogopa sana mtu mwenye hasira anayewakandamiza \q na kujiandaa kuwaangamiza. \q Iko wapi hasira hiyo sasa? Imetoweka!

decisions.choice: you have forgotten the LORD your Maker: fear of people comes from forgetting the Creator
decisions.reason: The one who made Israel also stretched out the sky and founded the earth (40:22; 42:5; 44:24). To fear a mortal oppressor is to forget how great he is.

decisions.choice: the oppressor: the power that holds the people captive, Babylon
decisions.reason: The word means one who presses hard or hems in. In these chapters the captor is Babylon (47:6; verse 14).

decisions.choice: where is the fury of the oppressor: a question that expects the answer that it is gone
decisions.reason: The question mocks the oppressor's rage as already past (compare 33:18). Verse 14 says the captive will soon be set free.

decisions.choice: It is gone!
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question implies.

source.text: מִהַ֥ר צֹעֶ֖ה לְהִפָּתֵ֑חַ וְלֹא־יָמ֣וּת לַשַּׁ֔חַת וְלֹ֥א יֶחְסַ֖ר לַחְמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: He will hasten, [one who is] stooping, to be released, and not he will die to the pit, and not he will lack his bread.

en.L: The one bowed down will hasten to be set free, \q and he will not die [and go down] to the pit, \q and he will not lack his bread.
en.B: The one bent low in chains will soon be released; \q he will not die and go down to the pit, \q nor will he go without bread.
en.R: Soon the prisoners will be set free. \q They will not die in prison or be buried in a grave. \q They will have enough food to eat.

es.L: El encorvado pronto será libertado, \q y no morirá [ni descenderá] a la fosa, \q ni le faltará su pan.
es.B: El que está encorvado bajo las cadenas pronto será liberado; \q no morirá ni bajará a la fosa, \q ni le faltará el pan.
es.R: Pronto los prisioneros serán liberados. \q No morirán en la cárcel ni serán enterrados en una tumba. \q Tendrán suficiente comida.

sw.L: Aliyeinama atafunguliwa upesi, \q wala hatakufa [na kushuka] shimoni, \q wala hatakosa mkate wake.
sw.B: Yule aliyepindika chini ya minyororo ataachiliwa hivi karibuni; \q hatakufa na kushuka shimoni, \q wala hatakosa mkate.
sw.R: Hivi karibuni wafungwa watawekwa huru. \q Hawatafia gerezani wala kuzikwa kaburini. \q Watakuwa na chakula cha kutosha.

decisions.choice: one bowed down: a captive bent under chains or in a cramped cell
decisions.reason: The word describes one stooping or bent low (63:1 uses it of one bending under his load). The context of the oppressor in verse 13 shows it is the prisoner of the exile (42:7, 22).

decisions.choice: the pit: the grave, or a pit used as a prison
decisions.reason: The word is used of the grave and the place of the dead (38:17; Psalm 16:10). A dry cistern could also serve as a prison (Jeremiah 38:6), so both senses may be in view.

decisions.choice: the prisoners; die in prison or be buried in a grave
decisions.reason: Readable explains the one bowed down as the prisoners, and gives both sides of the word for the pit.

source.text: וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ רֹגַ֣ע הַיָּ֔ם וַיֶּהֱמ֖וּ גַּלָּ֑יו יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I [am] Yahweh your God, [who] stirs up the sea and its waves roar; Yahweh of hosts [is] his name.

en.L: And I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q who stirs up the sea until its waves roar; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. \q I stir up the sea and make its waves roar. \q My name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

es.L: Y yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, \q que agito el mar y rugen sus olas; \q {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos [es] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.B: Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, \q que agito el mar hasta que rugen sus olas; \q {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.R: Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. \q Agito el mar y hago rugir sus olas. \q Mi nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

sw.L: Nami [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, \q ninayeichafua bahari hata mawimbi yake yanguruma; \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi [ndilo] jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.B: Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, \q ninayeichafua bahari mpaka mawimbi yake yanavuma; \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ndilo jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.R: Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. \q Ninaichafua bahari na kuyafanya mawimbi yake yangurume. \q Jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

decisions.choice: stirs up: churns the sea into a storm
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to stir up or to calm. The roaring waves that follow favor "stir up". Jeremiah 31:35 has the same line, and Job 26:12 uses the verb of God's power over the sea alongside Rahab.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts: the LORD who commands the armies of heaven
decisions.reason: See the note at 1:9.

decisions.choice: My name is the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself in the third person ("his name"). Readable puts it in the first person, as the rest of the verse is.

source.text: וָאָשִׂ֤ים דְּבָרַי֙ בְּפִ֔יךָ וּבְצֵ֥ל יָדִ֖י כִּסִּיתִ֑יךָ לִנְטֹ֤עַ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְלִיסֹ֣ד אָ֔רֶץ וְלֵאמֹ֥ר לְצִיּ֖וֹן עַמִּי־אָֽתָּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I have put my words in your mouth, and with the shadow of my hand I have covered you, to plant [the] heavens and to found [the] earth, and to say to Zion, my people [are] you.

en.L: And I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth, \q and in the shadow of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand I have covered you, \q to plant [the] heavens and to found [the] earth, \q and to say to Zion, "You [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people."
en.B: I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth \q and sheltered you in the shadow of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, \q to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, \q and to say to Zion, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people."
en.R: I have given you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words to speak. \q I have kept you safe, as if I were shading you with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand. \q I did this so that I could set the sky in place, make the earth firm, \q and say to the people of Zion, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people."

es.L: Y he puesto {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras en tu boca, \q y a la sombra de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano te he cubierto, \q para plantar los cielos y fundar la tierra, \q y para decir a Sion: «Tú [eres] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo».
es.B: He puesto {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras en tu boca \q y te he protegido a la sombra de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano, \q para plantar los cielos y poner los cimientos de la tierra, \q y para decirle a Sion: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo».
es.R: Te he dado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras para que las digas. \q Te he protegido, como si te diera sombra con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano. \q Hice esto para poner el cielo en su lugar, afirmar la tierra \q y decirle al pueblo de Sion: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo».

sw.L: Nami nimetia maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kinywani mwako, \q na katika kivuli cha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} nimekufunika, \q ili nizipande mbingu na kuiweka misingi ya dunia, \q na kuiambia Sayuni, "Wewe [ni] watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.B: Nimeweka maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kinywani mwako \q na kukuhifadhi katika kivuli cha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, \q ili kuzipanda mbingu na kuiweka misingi ya dunia, \q na kuiambia Sayuni, "Ninyi ni watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.R: Nimekupa maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} uyaseme. \q Nimekulinda, kana kwamba ninakutia kivulini kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Nilifanya hivyo ili niweke mbingu mahali pake, niifanye dunia imara, \q na kuwaambia watu wa Sayuni, "Ninyi ni watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."

decisions.choice: your mouth, covered you: the one addressed is Israel, or God's spokesman, the servant
decisions.reason: The same words are said of the servant in 49:2 ("in the shadow of his hand he hid me") and of the prophet's words in 59:21. Here "you" is masculine and is told it will say to Zion "You are my people", so it may be the servant or the prophet rather than the whole people.

decisions.choice: to plant the heavens: to set the heavens firmly in place
decisions.reason: The verb normally means to plant (a tree) or pitch (a tent). It is used here beside "found the earth"; verse 13 has "stretched out" the heavens instead. The planting may point to a new creation (65:17).

decisions.choice: you are my people: the covenant words
decisions.reason: These are the words of the covenant (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12; Hosea 2:25). The exile seemed to say "not my people" (Hosea 1:9); God now says the opposite.

decisions.choice: as if I were shading you; I did this so that
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hand's shadow and spells out the purpose clause.

source.text: הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י ק֚וּמִי יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁתִ֛ית מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־כּ֣וֹס חֲמָת֑וֹ אֶת־קֻבַּ֜עַת כּ֧וֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָ֛ה שָׁתִ֖ית מָצִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: Rouse yourself, rouse yourself, arise, Jerusalem, who have drunk from the hand of Yahweh the cup of his anger; the bowl of the cup of staggering you have drunk, you have drained.

en.L: Awake, awake, rise up, Jerusalem, \q you who have drunk from the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the cup of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath; \q the bowl, the cup of staggering, you have drunk [and] drained.
en.B: Awake, awake! Stand up, Jerusalem, \q you who have drunk from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s hand the cup of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath, \q who have drunk the goblet that makes people reel and emptied it to the bottom.
en.R: Wake up! Wake up! Get up, people of Jerusalem! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with you and punished you. It was as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made you drink a cup full of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. \q You drank every drop, and it made you stagger like someone who is drunk.

es.L: ¡Despierta, despierta, levántate, Jerusalén, \q tú que has bebido de la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} la copa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira; \q el cáliz, la copa del vértigo, has bebido [y] apurado!
es.B: ¡Despierta, despierta! ¡Ponte en pie, Jerusalén, \q tú que has bebido de la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} la copa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira, \q que has bebido el cáliz que hace tambalear y lo has vaciado hasta el fondo!
es.R: ¡Despierta! ¡Despierta! ¡Levántate, pueblo de Jerusalén! \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba enojado contigo y te castigó. Fue como si te hiciera beber una copa llena de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira. \q Te la bebiste hasta la última gota, y te hizo tambalear como a un borracho.

sw.L: Amka, amka, simama, Yerusalemu, \q wewe uliyekunywa kutoka mkononi mwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kikombe cha ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}; \q bakuli, kikombe cha kuyumbisha, umekinywa [na] kukimaliza.
sw.B: Amka, amka! Simama, Yerusalemu, \q wewe uliyekunywa kutoka mkononi mwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kikombe cha ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q uliyekunywa bilauri inayowafanya watu kuyumbayumba na kuimaliza hadi tone la mwisho.
sw.R: Amka! Amka! Simama, enyi watu wa Yerusalemu! \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwakasirikia na kuwaadhibu. Ilikuwa kana kwamba aliwanywesha kikombe kilichojaa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Mlikinywa chote, nacho kikawafanya mpepesuke kama mlevi.

decisions.choice: the cup of his wrath, the cup of staggering: God's judgment pictured as a drink that makes one reel
decisions.reason: God's anger is a cup he gives to drink, and those who drink it stagger like drunkards (Jeremiah 25:15-29; Psalm 75:9; Ezekiel 23:31-34). Jerusalem has drunk it in the fall of the city and the exile. Revelation 14:10 and 16:19 use the same picture.

decisions.choice: rouse yourself, rouse yourself: the call of verse 9 turned back on Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The people cried to the LORD's arm, "Awake, awake" (verse 9). Now God calls Jerusalem to wake up, with a form of the verb that means "rouse yourself". The same call comes again in 52:1.

decisions.choice: the bowl ... drained: drunk to the last drop
decisions.reason: The word for the bowl is a large cup or goblet, found only here and in verse 22. "Drained" means wrung out to the dregs (Psalm 75:9).

decisions.choice: Awake, awake
decisions.reason: The verb differs from the one in verse 9, but it has the same sense, so the same words are used to show that God answers the people's cry with his own.

decisions.choice: The LORD was angry with you and punished you. It was as if
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup stands for before giving the picture.

source.text: אֵין־מְנַהֵ֣ל לָ֔הּ מִכָּל־בָּנִ֖ים יָלָ֑דָה וְאֵ֤ין מַחֲזִיק֙ בְּיָדָ֔הּ מִכָּל־בָּנִ֖ים גִּדֵּֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: There is not [one] leading her from all [the] children she has borne, and there is not [one] taking hold of her hand from all [the] children she has brought up.

en.L: There is no [one] to guide her among all the {{gender:children|sons}} she has borne, \q and there is no [one] to take her by the hand among all the {{gender:children|sons}} she has raised.
en.B: Of all the {{gender:children|sons}} she bore, there is not one to guide her; \q of all the {{gender:children|sons}} she raised, there is no one to take her by the hand.
en.R: She had many children, but none of them is there to lead her home. \q She raised them, but not one of them takes her hand to help her walk.

es.L: No hay quien la guíe de entre todos los hijos que dio a luz, \q y no hay quien la tome de la mano de entre todos los hijos que crio.
es.B: De todos los hijos que dio a luz, no hay uno que la guíe; \q de todos los hijos que crio, no hay quien la tome de la mano.
es.R: Tuvo muchos hijos, pero ninguno está allí para llevarla a casa. \q Los crio, pero ninguno de ellos la toma de la mano para ayudarla a caminar.

sw.L: Hakuna [wa] kumwongoza miongoni mwa watoto wote aliowazaa, \q wala hakuna [wa] kumshika mkono miongoni mwa watoto wote aliowalea.
sw.B: Kati ya watoto wote aliowazaa, hakuna hata mmoja wa kumwongoza; \q kati ya watoto wote aliowalea, hakuna wa kumshika mkono.
sw.R: Alikuwa na watoto wengi, lakini hakuna hata mmoja aliyepo kumwongoza nyumbani. \q Aliwalea, lakini hakuna hata mmoja anayemshika mkono ili kumsaidia kutembea.

decisions.choice: no one to guide her, no one to take her by the hand: no child helps the reeling mother
decisions.reason: A mother who staggers needs her children to hold her up and lead her home; it was a child's duty to care for a parent. Jerusalem's children are themselves fallen (verse 20), so she has no help.

decisions.choice: her: the address to Jerusalem turns briefly to the third person
decisions.reason: Verse 17 spoke to Jerusalem as "you"; verse 18 speaks about her, then verse 19 returns to "you".

decisions.choice: hijos (no gender span)
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already includes daughters, so the English gender span (children / sons) has no Spanish counterpart, as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: watoto, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span on "children/sons". Swahili "watoto" already means sons and daughters alike, and "wana" would mean the same, so the setting has no wording to change here.

source.text: שְׁתַּ֤יִם הֵ֨נָּה֙ קֹֽרְאֹתַ֔יִךְ מִ֖י יָנ֣וּד לָ֑ךְ הַשֹּׁ֧ד וְהַשֶּׁ֛בֶר וְהָרָעָ֥ב וְהַחֶ֖רֶב מִ֥י אֲנַחֲמֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Two [things] these [have] befallen you; who will show sympathy to you? The devastation and the destruction, and the famine and the sword; who [as] I will comfort you?

en.L: These two [things] have happened to you; \q who will grieve with you? \q Ruin and destruction, famine and sword; how will I comfort you?
en.B: These two disasters have come upon you; \q who will grieve for you? \q Devastation and ruin, famine and sword: how can I comfort you?
en.R: Two kinds of trouble have come upon you. \q Your land was destroyed and ruined, and your people died from hunger and war. \q Who will feel sorry for you? How can I comfort you?

es.L: Estas dos [cosas] te han sobrevenido; \q ¿quién se condolerá de ti? \q La desolación y la destrucción, el hambre y la espada; ¿cómo te consolaré?
es.B: Estas dos desgracias han venido sobre ti; \q ¿quién llorará por ti? \q Devastación y ruina, hambre y espada: ¿cómo podré consolarte?
es.R: Dos clases de desgracias han caído sobre ti. \q Tu tierra fue destruida y arruinada, y tu gente murió de hambre y en la guerra. \q ¿Quién sentirá lástima por ti? ¿Cómo puedo consolarte?

sw.L: Mambo haya mawili yamekupata; \q ni nani atakayeomboleza pamoja nawe? \q Uharibifu na maangamizi, njaa na upanga; nitakufarijije?
sw.B: Maafa haya mawili yamekujia; \q ni nani atakayekuombolezea? \q Ukiwa na uharibifu, njaa na upanga: nitawezaje kukufariji?
sw.R: Aina mbili za taabu zimekupata. \q Nchi yako iliharibiwa na kuangamizwa, na watu wako walikufa kwa njaa na vita. \q Ni nani atakayekuonea huruma? Nitawezaje kukufariji?

decisions.choice: two things, four words: two pairs, ruin of the land and death of the people
decisions.reason: "Two" is followed by four words in two pairs: devastation and destruction strike the city and land; famine and sword strike its people.

decisions.choice: how will I comfort you: the standard Hebrew text has the first person
decisions.reason: The standard text reads literally "who, I comfort you?", best taken as "how will I comfort you?" (compare Amos 7:2, 5). The Great Isaiah Scroll and the Septuagint (from memory; to be checked) have "who will comfort you?", matching the earlier question in the verse. The standard text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Your land was destroyed and ruined, and your people died from hunger and war
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the two pairs and moves the first question after them.

source.text: בָּנַ֜יִךְ עֻלְּפ֥וּ שָׁכְב֛וּ בְּרֹ֥אשׁ כָּל־חוּצ֖וֹת כְּת֣וֹא מִכְמָ֑ר הַֽמְלֵאִ֥ים חֲמַת־יְהוָ֖ה גַּעֲרַ֥ת אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your children have fainted; they have lain at [the] head of all [the] streets like an antelope [in] a net, the [ones] full of the anger of Yahweh, the rebuke of your God.

en.L: Your {{gender:children|sons}} have fainted; they lie at the head of every street like an antelope [caught in] a net, \q full of the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the rebuke of your God.
en.B: Your {{gender:children|sons}} have collapsed; they lie at the corner of every street like an antelope in a net, \q filled to the brim with the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the rebuke of your God.
en.R: Your people have fainted. They lie at the corner of every street, like a wild animal caught in a net. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God was angry and punished them, and they could not take any more.

es.L: Tus hijos han desfallecido; yacen en la entrada de todas las calles como antílope en la red, \q llenos de la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, de la reprensión de tu Dios.
es.B: Tus hijos se han desmayado; yacen en la esquina de cada calle como un antílope en una red, \q llenos hasta el borde de la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, de la reprensión de tu Dios.
es.R: Tu gente se ha desmayado. Yace en la esquina de cada calle, como un animal salvaje atrapado en una red. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios estaba enojado y los castigó, y ya no podían más.

sw.L: Watoto wako wamezimia; wamelala katika kila pembe ya njia kama paa [aliyenaswa katika] wavu, \q wamejaa ghadhabu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, karipio la Mungu wako.
sw.B: Watoto wako wameanguka; wamelala katika kona ya kila njia kama paa katika wavu, \q wamejazwa ghadhabu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mpaka ukingoni, karipio la Mungu wako.
sw.R: Watu wako wamezimia. Wamelala katika pembe ya kila njia, kama mnyama wa porini aliyenaswa katika wavu. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako aliwakasirikia na kuwaadhibu, nao hawakuweza kustahimili zaidi.

decisions.choice: antelope: a wild animal of the oryx or antelope kind
decisions.reason: The word is listed among clean wild animals in Deuteronomy 14:5. Caught in a hunter's net, it struggles until it is exhausted.

decisions.choice: full of the wrath of the LORD: they have drunk the cup of verse 17 to the full
decisions.reason: The cup picture continues: Jerusalem's children are filled with God's anger as with strong drink and lie helpless (Jeremiah 13:13; Lamentations 2:11-12, 19).

decisions.choice: Your people; a wild animal; could not take any more
decisions.reason: Readable says "people" for the city's children, describes the antelope, and explains "full of the wrath".

source.text: לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְעִי־נָ֥א זֹ֖את עֲנִיָּ֑ה וּשְׁכֻרַ֖ת וְלֹ֥א מִיָּֽיִן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Therefore hear, please, this, afflicted [one], and drunken [one], and not from wine.

en.L: Therefore hear this, afflicted [one], \q drunk, but not with wine:
en.B: So hear this, you who are afflicted, \q you who are drunk but not with wine:
en.R: So listen to this, you poor, suffering people. \q You stagger like someone who is drunk, but not from drinking wine.

es.L: Por tanto, oye ahora esto, afligida, \q ebria, pero no de vino:
es.B: Así que escucha esto, tú que estás afligida, \q tú que estás ebria, pero no de vino:
es.R: Así que escucha esto, pobre pueblo que sufre. \q Te tambaleas como alguien que está borracho, pero no por haber bebido vino.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo sikia hili, [wewe] uliyeteswa, \q uliyelewa, lakini si kwa divai:
sw.B: Basi sikia hili, wewe uliyeteseka, \q wewe uliyelewa lakini si kwa divai:
sw.R: Kwa hiyo sikilizeni hili, enyi watu maskini mnaoteseka. \q Mnapepesuka kama mtu aliyelewa, lakini si kwa kunywa divai.

decisions.choice: drunk, but not with wine: staggering from God's judgment, not from drink
decisions.reason: The cup of wrath (verse 17) has made Jerusalem reel. The same expression is used in 29:9.

decisions.choice: therefore hear this: the turn to the promise of verses 22-23
decisions.reason: Because no one else comforts her (verses 18-19), God himself now speaks to Jerusalem.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנַ֣יִךְ יְהוָ֗ה וֵאלֹהַ֨יִךְ֙ יָרִ֣יב עַמּ֔וֹ הִנֵּ֥ה לָקַ֛חְתִּי מִיָּדֵ֖ךְ אֶת־כּ֣וֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָ֑ה אֶת־קֻבַּ֨עַת֙ כּ֣וֹס חֲמָתִ֔י לֹא־תוֹסִ֥יפִי לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֖הּ עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says your lord Yahweh, and your God [who] contends [for] his people: Here! I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering, the bowl of the cup of my anger; not you will repeat to drink it again.

en.L: Thus says your Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and your God, [who] pleads the cause of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people: \q Look, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering, \q the bowl, the cup of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath; \q you will not drink it again.
en.B: Your Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your God who takes up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people's cause, says this: \q See, I have taken out of your hand the cup that makes you reel. \q The goblet of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath you will never drink again.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your Master says, your God who defends {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people: \q Look, I have taken away the cup that made you stagger. \q I have taken the cup of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger from you. \q You will never have to drink from it again.

es.L: Así dice tu Señor, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y tu Dios, [que] defiende la causa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo: \q Mira, he quitado de tu mano la copa del vértigo, \q el cáliz, la copa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira; \q nunca más la beberás.
es.B: Tu Señor, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, tu Dios que defiende la causa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, dice esto: \q Mira, he quitado de tu mano la copa que te hace tambalear. \q El cáliz de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira nunca más lo beberás.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, tu Amo, tu Dios que defiende a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo: \q Mira, te he quitado la copa que te hacía tambalear. \q Te he quitado la copa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira. \q Nunca más tendrás que beber de ella.

sw.L: Bwana wako, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, asema hivi, na Mungu wako, [anayewatetea] watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: \q Tazama, nimekiondoa mkononi mwako kikombe cha kuyumbisha, \q bakuli, kikombe cha ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q hutakinywa tena.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo Bwana wako asemavyo, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wako anayeshika upande wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: \q Tazama, nimekitoa mkononi mwako kikombe kinachokuyumbisha. \q Bilauri ya ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} hutainywa tena kamwe.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Bwana wako analosema, Mungu wako anayewatetea watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: \q Tazama, nimekiondoa kikombe kilichokufanya upepesuke. \q Nimekiondoa kwako kikombe cha hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Hutakunywa tena kutoka kwake kamwe.

decisions.choice: your Lord: your master, the one you serve
decisions.reason: The word is plural in form, as titles of majesty often are, and means lord or master. Used with the divine name it says the LORD is Jerusalem's rightful master (compare 1:24; 26:13).

decisions.choice: who pleads the cause of his people: who argues his people's case as their advocate
decisions.reason: The verb is used of bringing a case at law. Here God takes his people's side (Jeremiah 50:34; Psalm 43:1), as the servant's helper did in 50:8.

decisions.choice: I have taken the cup; you will not drink it again: the judgment on Jerusalem is over
decisions.reason: The cup of verse 17 is taken away for good (40:2; 54:9). Verse 23 says where it goes next.

decisions.choice: your Master
decisions.reason: Readable says "Master" for the title meaning lord, so that it is not confused with the divine name.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֨יהָ֙ בְּיַד־מוֹגַ֔יִךְ אֲשֶׁר־אָמְר֥וּ לְנַפְשֵׁ֖ךְ שְׁחִ֣י וְנַעֲבֹ֑רָה וַתָּשִׂ֤ימִי כָאָ֨רֶץ֙ גֵּוֵ֔ךְ וְכַח֖וּץ לַעֹבְרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will put it in [the] hand of [those who] grieve you, who said to your soul, Bow down, and let us pass over; and you made like the ground your back, and like the street for [those] passing over.

en.L: And I will put it into the hand of your tormentors, \q who said to you, "Bow down, so that we may walk over [you]," \q and you made your back like the ground, \q and like the street for [those who] walk over [it].
en.B: I will put it into the hands of those who tormented you, \q who said to you, "Lie face down, so we can walk across you." \q And you made your back like the ground, \q like a street for people to walk on.
en.R: Now I will make the people who hurt you drink from that cup. \q They told you, "Lie down on the ground so we can walk on you." \q And you had to let them. Your back became like a road for them to walk on.

es.L: Y la pondré en la mano de tus atormentadores, \q que dijeron a tu alma: «Inclínate, para que pasemos [sobre ti]», \q y tú pusiste tu espalda como el suelo, \q y como la calle para los que pasaban.
es.B: La pondré en las manos de los que te atormentaron, \q que te dijeron: «Échate boca abajo para que pasemos por encima de ti». \q Y tú pusiste tu espalda como el suelo, \q como una calle para que la gente pasara.
es.R: Ahora haré que la gente que te hizo daño beba de esa copa. \q Te decían: «Échate al suelo para que caminemos sobre ti». \q Y tuviste que dejarlos. Tu espalda se convirtió en un camino para que caminaran sobre ella.

sw.L: Nami nitakitia mkononi mwa wanaokutesa, \q walioiambia nafsi yako, "Inama, ili tupite [juu yako]," \q nawe ukaufanya mgongo wako kama ardhi, \q na kama njia kwa [wale] wapitao.
sw.B: Nitakitia mikononi mwa wale waliokutesa, \q waliokuambia, "Lala kifudifudi ili tupite juu yako." \q Nawe ukaufanya mgongo wako kama ardhi, \q kama barabara ya watu kupita.
sw.R: Sasa nitawanywesha kikombe hicho watu waliokuumiza. \q Walikuambia, "Lala chini ili tutembee juu yako." \q Nawe ilikubidi uwaache. Mgongo wako ukawa kama barabara ya kupita.

decisions.choice: bow down so we may walk over you: conquerors treading on the backs of the defeated
decisions.reason: Victors in the ancient world sometimes made captives lie down and walked or rode over them, as a sign of complete defeat (Joshua 10:24; Psalm 66:12; 129:3).

decisions.choice: said to your soul: said to you
decisions.reason: "Your soul" here means "you yourself", as often in Hebrew. It may also suggest they spoke to crush her spirit.

decisions.choice: I will put it in the hand of your tormentors: the cup passes to the oppressors
decisions.reason: The judgment Jerusalem drank now goes to those who abused her (47:6; Jeremiah 25:15-17, 26).

decisions.choice: make the people who hurt you drink from that cup
decisions.reason: Readable says what putting the cup in their hand means.
